questions.stem_md: At the beginning of a season, the coach of a junior boys' rugby team recorded the weight (in kg) of each player in his team and the number of push-ups that each player was able to do in one minute. The data is represented in the table and scatter plot below. The least squares regression line for the data is drawn.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of the least squares regression line for the data.
Write down the correlation coefficient.

The coach uses the least squares regression line to set the target for the minimum number of push-ups by each team member according to their weight. Predict the number of push-ups that a member of the team, who weighs $29$ kg, should do to meet the target.
Write down the mean number of push-ups for the given data.

The players trained hard during the season. At the end of the season, the coach reported that each player was able to do $5$ more push-ups per minute than they did at the beginning of the season. How does the increase in the number of push-ups influence the standard deviation of the data?

At the beginning of the season, the coach used the least squares regression line as the minimum target for a player to aim for. Determine the maximum possible increase in the number of push-ups that a team member must obtain to reach the minimum target.
questions.notes: Wording kept as printed. Read from the scatter plot as the largest distance of a point below the regression line; no dedicated residual skill.

questions.stem_md: The cumulative frequency graph (ogive) shows the time taken (in minutes) for $60$ employees to travel to work each morning.

questions.text_md: Estimate the median travel time.
Estimate the lower quartile.
Estimate the interquartile range.

The minimum and maximum times taken for an employee to travel to work are $5$ and $120$ minutes respectively. On the scaled line in the ANSWER BOOK, draw a box and whisker diagram to indicate the distribution of the data as represented in the ogive above.

The company manager decided that all employees who travel for an hour or more will be allowed to work from home for part of the day. What percentage of the employees will be allowed to work from home for part of the day?

questions.stem_md:
Employees work $8$ hours in a normal working day. The manager decided the following rule for time to work from home:

- An employee is allowed to work half an hour from home for each time interval of $20$ minutes, or part thereof, above an hour taken to travel to work.
questions.text_md: On a certain day, an employee takes $110$ minutes to travel to work. Calculate the number of minutes that this employee will be allowed to work from home on this day.
questions.notes: Rule-based word problem with no statistics skill; tagged with alg.words-to-equations (no better fit in the skill graph).

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, $\triangle ACD$ has vertices $A$, $D(3\,;\,-9)$ and $C(-9\,;\,0)$, where $A$ is a point in the second quadrant. $B(-1\,;\,k)$ lies on side $DC$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the gradient of $DC$.
Determine the equation of $DC$ in the form $y=mx+c$.
Show that $k=-6$.
Calculate the length of $DC$.
Calculate the ratio of $\dfrac{DB}{DC}$.
If $M$ is a point on $AD$ such that $AC\parallel MB$, calculate the ratio of $\dfrac{\text{Area }\triangle MBD}{\text{Area }\triangle ACD}$.
questions.notes: Analytical-geometry diagram but a Euclidean-geometry ratio question (proportion/area); tagged with the euc skills.

questions.text_md: If it is further given that the gradient of $AD$ is $-4$ and the length of $AD$ is $\sqrt{612}$ units, calculate the coordinates of $A$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $M(1\,;\,3)$ is the centre of the circle. The circle cuts the $x$-axis at $N$. $ST$ is a tangent to the circle at $P(3\,;\,9)$. $R(d\,;\,1)$, with $d>0$, and $L$ lie on the circle. $O$ and $V$ are the $x$-intercepts of $PL$ and $RL$ respectively.

questions.text_md: Write down the coordinates of $L$.
questions.notes: $PL$ passes through the centre $M$ (as drawn), so $M$ is the midpoint of $PL$.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of tangent $ST$ to the circle at $P$.
Show that the equation of the circle with centre $M$ is $x^{2}+y^{2}-2x-6y-30=0$.
Show that $d=7$.
Calculate the size of $\hat{L}$.
questions.notes: Angle $\hat{L}$ is the angle between $LP$ and $LR$ (the angle at $L$ in triangle $PLR$ as drawn).

questions.text_md: $TR$ is a tangent to the circle at $R$. Prove that $PT\perp RT$.

questions.stem_md:
In the diagram, line $OP$ is given with $P(-3\,;\,-4)$. $K\hat{O}P=A$.

Determine, **without using a calculator**, the value of:

questions.text_md: $\cos A$
$\cos 2A$
$\sin(A-B)$, if it is further given that $\sin B=\dfrac{4}{5}$ and $90^\circ<B<360^\circ$

If $\cos\alpha=p$, express the following expression in terms of $p$:

$$\dfrac{\cos\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}-45^\circ\right)\sin\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2}-45^\circ\right)}{2}$$

questions.stem_md: Given the identity: $\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y$

questions.text_md: Use the compound angle identity given above to derive a formula for $\cos(x+y)$.

Hence, or otherwise, show that:

$$\dfrac{\cos(90^\circ-x)\cos y+\sin(-y)\cos(180^\circ+x)}{\cos x\cos(360^\circ+y)+\sin(360^\circ-x)\sin y}=\tan(x+y)$$
Solve for $x$ in the interval $x\in(0^\circ\,;\,360^\circ)$ if $f(x)=2$.
Calculate the maximum value of $g$.
Write down the smallest possible value of $x$ for which $g$ will have a maximum value in the interval $x\in(0^\circ\,;\,360^\circ]$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, the graph of $f(x)=\tan x$ is drawn for the interval $x\in[-180^\circ\,;\,180^\circ]$.

questions.text_md: Write down the equation of the asymptote of $f$ in the interval $x\in[0^\circ\,;\,180^\circ]$.
Write down the values of $x$ in the interval $x\in[-180^\circ\,;\,0^\circ]$ for which $f(x)\leq 0$.
Write down the period of $g$.

On the grid given in the ANSWER BOOK, draw the graph of $g(x)=\cos 2x+1$ for the interval $x\in[-180^\circ\,;\,180^\circ]$. Clearly show the intercepts with the axes as well as the coordinates of the turning points.
Use the graphs to determine the general solution of $2\cos^{3}x-\sin x=0$.
questions.notes: Printed as $2\cos^3 x-\sin x=0$ (checked at 300 dpi): dividing by $\cos x$ gives $2\cos^2 x=\tan x$, i.e. $\cos 2x+1=\tan x$, so the graphs of $f$ and $g$ are used.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $C$ is the foot of a vertical building and $D$ is the top of the same building. The height of the building, $CD$, is $16$ m. Two observers are standing $19$ m apart at points $A$ and $B$, where $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie in the same horizontal plane. A painter is working at point $E$ on the building. The angle of elevation of $D$ from $A$ is $46{,}85^\circ$. $D\hat{E}B=122^\circ$ and $B\hat{C}A=105{,}61^\circ$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the length of $AC$, the distance between the observer at $A$ and the foot of the building.
Calculate how far the painter at $E$ is from the top of the building.

questions.stem_md:
Provide reasons for your statements in QUESTIONS 9, 10 and 11.

In the diagram, $ABCD$ is a cyclic quadrilateral. $BC$ is produced to $E$. $AC$ is drawn. $\hat{A}_1=\dfrac{1}{2}\hat{B}$, $\hat{A}_2=46^\circ$ and $\hat{C}_1=86^\circ$.

questions.text_md: Calculate, with a reason, the value of $\hat{A}_1$.
Hence, prove that $AD=DC$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\triangle RST$ is drawn. Line $AB$ intersects $RS$ and $RT$ at $A$ and $B$ respectively such that $AB\parallel ST$.
questions.text_md: Prove the theorem which states that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally, i.e. $\dfrac{RA}{AS}=\dfrac{RB}{BT}$

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $O$ is the centre of the circle. $\triangle PWS$ is drawn with $P$, $W$ and $S$ on the circle. $OR\perp PS$. $PRS$ is produced to $T$. $SW$ and $OT$ intersect at $V$. $OV:OT=1:4$

questions.text_md: Prove, with reasons, that $OR:WS=1:2$
Calculate the length of $PT$ if $ST=15$ units.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $A$, $B$, $G$ and $F$ lie on the larger circle. A smaller circle is drawn to touch the larger circle internally at $A$. $EA$ is a common tangent to both circles. $EBCF$ is a tangent to the smaller circle at $C$. $AC$ is produced to $G$. $AF$ cuts the smaller circle at $D$. $AB$, $CD$ and $GF$ are drawn.

questions.text_md: If $E\hat{A}G=x$, determine with reasons, FOUR other angles that are equal to $x$.
Prove that $AG\cdot AD=AC\cdot AF$
questions.notes: The printed multiplication dots in $AG.AD=AC.AF$ are transcribed as $\cdot$.

questions.text_md: Prove that $\triangle AGF\,|||\,\triangle ABC$
questions.notes: The paper uses $|||$ for similarity (as in 2025 P2 Q11.2.2).

questions.text_md: Prove that $GF^{2}=\dfrac{BC\cdot FC\cdot AF}{AD}$
questions.notes: The printed multiplication dots in $BC.FC.AF$ are transcribed as $\cdot$.
